title: Blind baking, the proper method
subtitle: Pre-baking a pastry case without its filling so the base cooks through
excerpt: Blind baking pre-cooks a pastry case before adding a wet filling. Without it, the base stays raw and soggy underneath custard, cream, or lemon curd. The method requires baking paper and weights to hold the pastry flat, then a further few minutes uncovered to dry and colour the base.
sourceNotes: Blind baking is a standard pastry technique documented across British and French baking traditions. The method of using dried beans or ceramic weights to hold the pastry flat is the widely accepted home approach.

recipe.yieldDescription: Technique for any lined pastry tin
recipe.makeAheadNotes: A blind-baked shell can be stored in an airtight tin for up to 2 days before filling.

glossaryTerms.definition: Pre-baking a pastry case without its filling, lined with baking paper and weighted down with baking beans to prevent the base from puffing up and the sides from slumping.
A pastry base that is undercooked or waterlogged from a wet filling. Prevented by blind baking and ensuring the filling is not too liquid when added to the shell.

. The weights hold the pastry flat during the first bake. Remove them for the second stage to dry and colour the base.

Roll the pastry 3 to 4 mm thick on a lightly floured surface. Roll it up loosely onto the rolling pin and unroll it over the tin. Press the pastry gently into the base and sides without stretching it, stretched pastry shrinks back in the oven. Trim the overhanging edge flush with the rim or leave a 5 mm overlap and crimp. Prick the base all over with a fork.

Rest the lined tin in the fridge for 20 to 30 minutes. Cold pastry shrinks less than warm pastry and holds its shape better in the oven. Preheat the oven to 190°C (conventional) while the pastry chills.
Line the pastry case with a sheet of baking paper, pushing it into the corners. Fill with
or dried pulses to a depth of about 2 cm. Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes, until the edges are pale gold and the sides look set.

Remove the paper and beans carefully, they will be hot. Return the case to the oven for 8 to 10 minutes, until the base looks matte and feels dry to a gentle touch. It should be pale gold, not raw, but not deeply coloured (it bakes further with the filling).

If any cracks appear after the beans come out, brush the inside of the hot shell with beaten egg yolk and return it to the oven for 2 minutes. The egg sets and seals the crack before the filling goes in.
